statement: Atomic intent does not imply atomic completion.
Consensus does not imply atomic completion.
Distributed admissibility does not imply atomic completion.
Atomic completion does not imply settlement finality.
Atomic completion does not imply continuity preservation.
Atomic partiality does not create repair authority.
Atomic indeterminate is distinct from atomic partial, no-effect, and complete.
Distributed partial effect maps to inherited F1 PARTIAL rather than redefining it.
Endpoint economic equivalence does not establish historically atomic execution.
Compensation following partial distributed settlement is a new consequential execution.
Reversal does not erase prior partial distributed execution.
Partiality and conflict are distinct properties.
Partial distributed settlement does not establish settlement finality.
